test_title: SSC CHSL (2022) Tier-II Official Paper (Held On: 26 Jun, 2023 Shift 1).
subject: general
question: In May 2023, the Supreme Court of India granted couples the right to get divorce on the grounds of ‘irretrievable breakdown of marriage’ under ______ of the Indian Constitution.
solution:
The correct asnwer is __**Article 142(1).**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **May 2023**, the Supreme Court of India used **Article 142(1) **of the Indian Constitution to grant couples the **right to divorce based on 'irretrievable breakdown of marriage'.**
 
• **Article 142(1) **of the Indian Constitution reads, **"The Supreme Court in the exercise of its jurisdiction may pass such decree or make such order as is necessary for doing complete justice in any cause or matter pending before it...".**
 
• The Supreme Court's decision expanded the grounds on which divorce can be sought in India.
 
• Previously, the grounds for divorce were outlined in** individual personal laws and did not include the concept of 'irretrievable breakdown of marriage'** as it was not explicitly listed as grounds for divorce in any specific legislation.** The 2023 ruling made it a valid reason to seek a divorce.**
 
• The court used its discretionary powers to take cognizance of the realities of irreparable marriages and rule in favor of allowing legal terminations in such cases. This action sets a significant precedent for future cases involving such marital situations.
 
• This step by the Supreme Court could potentially pave the **way for broader legal reform, rooting the law** more firmly in the changing social context and conditions of the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 132(1):**

 
 
• **Article 132(1) **of the Indian Constitution is in **Part V **that deals with **'The Union.'**
 
• This article ensures that **crucial questions of law being decided by the High Court can be reviewed by the Supreme Court if necessary.**
 
• This helps maintain consistency in the interpretation of laws across the country and the** binding nature** of Supreme Court judgments.
 
 
 
• **Article 122(1):**
 
 
• **Article 122** of the Indian Constitution discusses the** "Courts not to inquire into proceedings of Parliament."**
 
• **Article 122(1)** states,** "The validity of any proceedings in Parliament shall not be called in question on the ground of any alleged irregularity of procedure."**
 
• The purpose of this provision is to uphold the **principle of separation of powers, an essential feature of the Constitution.**
 
 
 
• **Article 152:**
 
 
• Article 152 only defines the term **"Governor"** as referenced in** Part VI** of the Constitution, which deals with the states.
